claim: REFUTED BY ITSELF: patching T12c's single residual entry with a unit term does NOT yield a new rank-23 anchor.

constructionAttempted.reading: under idx(3,i,j) = 3i+j the triple (7,4,7) is a=(2,1), b=(1,1), c=(2,1), i.e. exactly the naive term of (i,j,k)=(2,1,1)
constructionAttempted.patch: append the unit term e_7 (x) e_4 (x) e_7
constructionAttempted.resultBeforeCheck: reported by checker.verify() as correct=true, rank=23, mismatches=0, and also correct over F_2
constructionAttempted.resultAfterCheck: the resulting 23-term scheme is T11_solution re-sorted; it is NOT a new anchor

refutation.method: canonical triple keys (u,v,w) joined, compared as SETS
refutation.conclusion: the patch term e_7 (x) e_4 (x) e_7 is ALREADY one of T11's 23 terms, so T12c's residual is precisely one of T11's own terms and adding it back returns T11 itself

whyTheErrorWasAlmostMissed.symptom: the band screen returned digit-identical refutation counts for the patched scheme and for T11 at k = 2,3,4,5 (253/253, 1767+4, 8503+349, 29199+4254)
whyTheErrorWasAlmostMissed.reading: treated at first as a coincidence of counting, and as the confirmation that the new base was a genuinely different support with the same statistics
whyTheErrorWasAlmostMissed.actualCause: it was the same support. Identical counts were the tell, not the confirmation.

whatThisCloses.route: construct a NEW rank-23 base by repairing a rank-22 near-miss with a single unit term, then screen its band as fresh ground
whatThisCloses.verdict: CLOSED for the T12c near-miss: every unit-term repair returns a landed anchor rather than a new base
whatThisCloses.scope: this refutes the unit-term patch on T12c only. It does NOT refute repairs of other near-misses by non-unit terms, and it is not a bound on the rank of 3x3 multiplication

whatSurvives.soundStatement: for an EXACT base B and a drop set K of size k, any completion with j fresh rank-1 terms has modpFlatDim(D_K) <= flatDim_over_Q(D_K) <= j, and reaching rank <= 22 from rank 23 forces j <= k - 1. So modpFlatDim(D_K) > k - 1 refutes the ENTIRE add-j family at once, with no coefficient, sparsity or factor ansatz assumed.
whatSurvives.knownAnswerControl: closes k=2 (253/253) and k=3 (1771/1771) on all four landed anchors, matching the campaign's own closure; at k=4 it reduces 8855 rows to exactly 3 per anchor
whatSurvives.measuredLimit: the 3 surviving k=4 rows per anchor all have a 7-entry deficit with L1 = 7 (a signed perfect matching) and exact flattening rank exactly 3 = addLimit. The flattening bound is therefore exactly tight on them and provably cannot refute them; a split-refined or box-cover stage is required, which is what R76 supplied.
whatSurvives.boundsUntouched: 19 <= R <= 23 over Q/R and 21 <= R <= 23 over F_2
